data.narrative:
Manastu Space is a Series A-stage space and aerospace company founded by Tushar Jadhav and Ashtesh Kumar that has raised $6M to date. The valuation universe comprises 5 public comparables (RKLB, PL, LUNR, ASTS, SATL) and 8 private peers including SpaceX, Rocket Lab, ICEYE, Sierra Space, and Planet Labs, representing a fragmented but data-rich sector.

Stage-progression analysis is the applicable triangulation method for this engagement. Using total capital raised ($6M) as a baseline proxy and applying a 2.0x step-up multiplier typical of Series A to early-growth-stage advancement, this method implies a post-money valuation of $12M. Public-comp anchoring cannot be applied without disclosed revenue figures, which private companies rarely publish. Peer-median benchmarking is inapplicable due to insufficient same-stage or adjacent-stage comparables meeting statistical threshold (0 same-stage, 2 adjacent-stage, 0 similar-tier observations; minimum 3 required). The public Space & Aerospace median P/S ratio stands at 27.4x across six tickers, but remains unusable without target revenue.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $10M to $14M, with a central point of $12M. This single-method foundation introduces material uncertainty. Critical gaps include absence of revenue or unit economics, insufficient private peer data at identical stage and comparable scale, and reliance on a generalized stage-progression multiplier rather than company-specific fundamentals. The range should be treated as indicative pending additional operational metrics and closer peer alignment.
